articles.title: In 2000, Pierce Brosnan bought two Malibu plots for his Orchid House: a 13,000-square-foot marvel of sustainability
articles.summary: Explore how Pierce Brosnan's Orchid House embodies sustainable luxury in Malibu, featuring eco-friendly design and unique elements inspired by Thai and Balinese architecture.
articles.body: The ‘James Bond’ actor Pierce Brosnan once bought two large plots in Malibu with his dream house in mind. The beloved actor invested a lot of time and money into creating his dream home, with sustainability at the forefront. The Orchid House is one of the earliest examples of the sustainable and eco-friendly homes that celebrities invested in. Here is a look into the actor’s real estate profile and one of the best examples of how seriously some stars take their responsibility toward the environment and climate.Pierce Brosnan bought two Malibu plots in 2000Pierce Brosnan made the big purchase of two plots of land in Malibu along with his wife, Keely Shaye Smith. The two invested USD 5.1 million and USD 2.25 million simply to buy the land and the original mid-century ranch house built on one of the plots. However, the couple wanted to start from scratch and demolished the home soon after finalising the purchase.Second Shelters further reported that this was followed by long, hard, and continuous work from the couple and their team of contractors over 12 years to build what everyone now knows as Orchid House, or ‘eco-mansion.’ The home was directly inspired by Thai and Balinese themes, an ode to the country after Brosnan fell in love with the place in 1997 while filming for ‘Tomorrow Never Dies.’More about Pierce Brosnan’s complete Orchid HouseThe complete compound now spans more than an acre, with around 117 feet of ocean frontage. The main house, along with the guest house, has wide plank teak flooring and scissor-truss ceilings. One thing the star and his partner prioritised in their dream home was windows. The entire space is covered with windows where they can let in fresh sunlight.How Pierce Brosnan made the Orchid House sustainableOne main aspect of the home comes from multiple features the actor installed during the building process that make it extremely eco-friendly. These features include an on-site water recycling plant, along with low-flow toilets, custom energy-saving lighting throughout the compound, and a solar-powered compost heap that turns itself. Solar panels across the house are directly connected to the pool and guest cabana, which can help heat the area up. Not only that, but he also has a system in place where unused energy can be sold off to the power grid if not needed.Pierce Brosnan’s Orchid House once reached a valuation of USD 100 millionBrosnan had invested around USD 8 million into the plots and a lot more money into building the home over the years; he first listed the property for USD 100 million in 2020. A year later, after failing to secure a potential buyer, he took the house off the market.Now, only two days ago, Brosnan and Keely confirmed that after having the home for around 26 years, they are ready to part ways with their Southeast Asian-inspired home. While talking to The Times, the couple shared that the frequent wildfires and other natural disasters in the area are a major factor in why they wish to sell. They added, “We’ve been spared by the fires a few times now. But I think it’s time to move. Everything changes; everything falls apart. We live by this body of earth’s water on a fault in a ring of earthquakes. That creates a fear.”Since their sons, Paris, 25, and Dylan, 29, have moved out, the couple has also embraced a simpler life and spends most of their days in Keely’s native Hawaii. He explained that they have a cottage in Kauai where they reside now, adding that it is a “little three-bedroom cottage at the end of the road. We have our own chickens, and I have a yurt where I paint.”Brosnan also commented on how many things in their life in Malibu have changed. He shared, “There have been doldrums. I have this beautiful house in Malibu. I have to pay the mortgage. There are school fees,” he explained to The Times. “There are definite moments of, oh, this boat is not quite sinking, but [it might] if we don’t get a job soon. I think the two of us are somewhat reclusive. It’s a long way into town. We have a small circle of friends here, but people get divorced, they die, and they move on. And we’re still here.”In 2020, when they first put the house on the market, Brosnan had also commented, “It’s time to move on… It’s time to change.” The two are ready to sell the house.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: The four-hour-long Elon Musk documentary might be preaching to the choir
articles.summary: After making documentaries on everything from Theranos to Steve Jobs, director Alex Gibney has turned his attention to Elon Musk.
articles.body: It makes sense that Musk is a long film. The latest from Alex Gibney, who has previously directed documentaries about Theranos and Steve Jobs, is an impressively thorough retelling of the story of Elon Musk, from his early days as a dot-com millionaire to “taking a wood chipper” to vital US government departments. In order to understand Musk’s rise to power, you need to know the whole story. Musk tells it compellingly and convincingly, but doesn’t offer much in the way of revelations if you’re aware of Musk’s catastrophic influence on the world. For everyone else, a demanding runtime just shy of four hours might prove too much of a barrier to being convinced. The film opens with shots of space and a voiceover of Musk detailing some of his sci-fi ambitions. From there, it’s a fairly chronological narrative of how we got to this point. The first section of the film reveals how Musk’s mythology was built, while also steadily seeding doubts that he’s the Tony Stark–style tycoon that many believe him to be. It starts off with the basic details, like when Musk was ousted as CEO from PayPal or how he convinced the world he founded Tesla, a company that existed before he was involved. The film juxtaposes his many bombastic claims about autonomous vehicles with visceral footage of a deadly crash involving a Tesla on autopilot. It drops in poignant interviews, like when former MAGA influencer Ashley St Clair, mother to one of Musk’s many children, declares in a terrified voice: “Elon is a nuke.” At the outset, Gibney makes it clear that his goal is to answer two questions with interrelated answers: how Musk got so powerful, and why we allowed it to happen. By gradually accruing power through Tesla, X, SpaceX, and Starlink, Musk ingratiated himself with governments all over the world, in particular the US, and then used that political power to further his own interests once it became so hard to extricate his influence. The documentary lays out the plot clearly and concisely, all in one place. [Media: Musk himself didn’t participate in the documentary. Instead, he sent Gibney a legal threat over it. So Gibney built in a digital doppelgänger that mouths to audio of things Musk actually said, based on a database the team created of existing clips. The avatar Musk veers into uncanny valley territory, with its overly expressive face and unsettling heavy breathing, but it’s a smart way of putting Musk’s face to his words, in a manner of speaking. And it fits well with Musk’s belief in simulation theory. Additionally, the movie uses plenty of sim and video game imagery to illustrate things throughout, like a fictional first-person shooter that depicts Musk dismantling Twitter and the US government with a chainsaw that shoots lasers. It’s over-the-top and absurd, but then again we’re here, in part, because of a kid bureaucrat named Big Balls. In many ways, Musk is successful. It lays out how he got to power and why he was able to accrue so much of it without being stopped, which boils down to him being far too rich and ingrained by the time most people realized what was going on. Unfortunately, as someone who has followed the story over the years, I can’t say I learned much or gained new insights into the man while watching Musk. Which makes me wonder who this film is for. Many people have already woken up to the fact that Musk is something quite different than some kind of genius inventor, but there are still plenty who only associate his name with past wins like incremental advances in reusable rockets or pre-Tesla Cybertruck vehicles. The film even interviews one fan who says he intentionally ignores the things about Musk that he doesn’t agree with. That’s exactly the kind of person who would benefit most from watching Musk lay it out all in one place. But in a world of dwindling attention spans, four hours in a theater is a lot to ask (even if it does have a 10-minute intermission). It could miss the people who need to see it the most. Musk is in theaters on October 16th. This review is based on a screening at the Toronto International Film Festival.

articles.title: Macklemore Dropped From Ed Sheeran Tour After Onstage ‘Free Palestine’ Statements
articles.summary: “We have been notified by venues on the upcoming U.S. tour dates that they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup,” promoter sa...
articles.body:
Macklemore has been removed from the rest of Ed Sheeran's stadium tour after several venues allegedly told the trek's promoter that they would not allow the rapper to perform. The news came after Macklemore made several onstage statements in support of Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank and called for a "free Palestine."

In an exclusive statement shared with Rolling Stone , Messina Touring Group, promoter of the U.S. leg of Sheeran's Loop Tour, said: "As the concert promoter for Ed Sheeran's U.S. Loop Tour, we have been notified by venues on the upcoming U.S. tour dates that they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup, which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans. After discussions with stakeholders, Macklemore will not be performing on the remaining support dates."

Macklemore was slated to appear at eight of the 10 shows left on the U.S. leg of Sheeran's tour, which is set to resume this Friday, Sept. 19, in Philadelphia. The venues that allegedly objected to the rapper include: Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia; Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts; Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta; Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis; Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, North Carolina; AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas; and Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Florida.

Reps for Sheeran and most of the venues did not immediately reply to requests for comment.

In a statement shared on Instagram , Macklemore claimed he was dropped from the tour after Robert Kraft — the billionaire owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium — mounted a pressure campaign against Sheeran.

"Ed told me that Kraft said I would not be allowed to perform in his stadium," Macklemore wrote. "Ed also told me that Kraft had rallied some of the other stadium owners and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: if Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues." (Reps for Kraft and the Kraft Group did not return requests for comment.)

Macklemore — who's been an outspoken supporter of Palestinians and those in Gaza for several years — joined the Loop Tour earlier this month, performing two shows at MetLife Stadium outside of New York City, on Sept. 4 and 5. At the first show, the Seattle rapper yelled "Free Palestine" onstage and expressed solidarity with people in Gaza and the occupied West Bank. He also showed images from the devastation in Gaza and performed his protest song, "Hind's Hall," about pro-Palestine demonstrators at Columbia, who occupied a building and named it after Hind Raja, a six-year-old killed by the Israeli military .

"A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very near and dear to my heart: 'Free Palestine,'" he said during the first MetLife show. "I said, 'Free Palestine!' I want those words to be loud and clear, so that people all the way in Gaza to the occupied West Bank know that we have not forgotten about them."

This spurred much criticism and backlash from pro-Israel groups. StopAntisemitism accused the rapper of ambushing fans with "anti-Israel propaganda" in an Instagram post, which the pop singer Pink amplified .

Pink later explained that she did not object to Macklemore's calls for a "Free Palestine," but said, "I have never asked for another artist to be silenced and I'm not asking now. I don't need anyone fired, and I don't need a refund. What I need is to be able to say, as a Jewish mom, 'that scared me, and it scared people I love,' without being told our fear is just propaganda, and without being told I'm somehow cool with genocide because I noticed?"

Additionally, the Israeli American Council launched a petition demanding Sheeran remove Macklemore from the rest of the tour, claiming his actions raised questions over "where the line should be drawn when an opening act uses a global concert platform to advance a one-sided political agenda."

At the second MetLife show, Macklemore reiterated his calls for a "Free Palestine" and addressed Jewish members of the audience, saying, "Criticism of Israel, criticism of apartheid, being against genocide in no way is a criticism of you. My message is for peace; love for all human beings to be treated with dignity, respect, and equality." (Humanitarian groups and a United Nations commission have said Israel's actions in Gaza constitute a genocide. Israel and its allies, including the United States, have denied this.)

Most of the stadiums that allegedly would not allow a Macklemore show did not immediately return requests for comments either, including for explanations as to why they objected to the rapper performing at their venue. While two of those stadiums are privately owned — Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte and Gillette Stadium in Foxborough — the rest are owned and, in many cases, operated by cities, states, or other government entities, potentially raising First Amendment issues if the venues barred Macklemore over his statements.

The last stop on Sheeran's Loop Tour, for instance, is Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, which found itself in a similar spot earlier this summer after booking two Kanye West concerts. The shows, unsurprisingly, drew backlash and calls for cancellation due to West's many past antisemitic statements, but they went ahead as planned.

Pointedly, Ye's promoter included a clause in his contract prohibiting Raymond James Stadium from canceling the gigs based on the rapper's past public statements or viewpoints. But legal experts also told local news that canceling the shows would've likely violated the First Amendment. Because Raymond James is owned by Hillsborough County, Florida, and operated by a public board, the Tampa Sports Authority, any cancellation based on Ye's past statements could have been seen as the government restricting speech.

When reached for comment on the Macklemore decision, a rep for the Tampa Sports Authority told Rolling Stone , "We can confirm Macklemore will not be performing at the upcoming show. Apart from this lineup change, the concert will go forward as planned."

Elsewhere in his statement on the matter, Macklemore called Sheeran a "friend" and acknowledged the singer-songwriter "was in a fucked up position" after the alleged pressure campaign. Macklemore continued: "His typical apolitical stance was being challenged in a way it never had been before. He told me that the words 'Free Palestine' and the image of the Palestinian flag were hurtful to a lot of people he spoke with. I told him that if those words were more offensive than tens of thousands of Palestinian children being killed by Israel, then there was a fundamental disconnect between where those people stood and where I stood. But he couldn't get past his public facing, 'I don't take sides.'"

The North American leg of Sheeran's Loop Tour is set to run through the fall, wrapping Nov. 7 at Raymond James Stadium. During the trek, Sheeran will continue to receive support from Lukas Graham and Aaron Rowe. A South American leg of the Loop Tour will follow in November and December.

This story was updated at 1:03 p.m. ET with quotes from a statement released by Macklemore.

articles.title: 'Dhurandhar ne satyanash kar diya,' says lyricist Sameer Anjaan as he slams the film for using old songs: 'They recreated my song while they are firing guns'
articles.summary: Veteran lyricist Sameer Anjaan–the man behind songs like Kuch Kuch Hota Hai and Tum Dil Ki Dhadkan Mein – recently slammed Ranveer Singh-starrer Dhura.
articles.body: Veteran lyricist Sameer Anjaan–the man behind songs like Kuch Kuch Hota Hai and Tum Dil Ki Dhadkan Mein – recently slammed Ranveer Singh-starrer Dhurandhar for using old songs in the background of sequences filled with violence. In a recent interview, he expressed disappointment over the way Bollywood has been treating music, arguing that experienced lyricists are often dismissed as being out of touch with the pulse of today’s generation.In a lengthy conversation with Komal Nahta on his YouTube podcast Game Changers, Sameer said, “Songs today don’t have meaning because the people today don’t have emotions and depth left in them. Cinema often mirrors society. With the introduction of OTT and other mediums, they are only paying attention to sex and violence and have sidelined music.”Remembering the days when producers and directors paid close attention to every song in their films, Sameer recalled working on Kuch Kuch Hota Hai. He said, “I still remember, when I was writing the title song Kuch Kuch Hota Hai, Karan Johar gave me a narration of over six hours with details including what Shah Rukh Khan and Kajol would be wearing in the song sequence.”He blamed the entry of corporate culture into filmmaking for affecting creativity and attention to detail.“The entry of corporate has also given rise to bad content. People now approach us without any context. They randomly say, ‘Koi hit gaana hai toh dedo.’ Not like we walk with a hit song in our pocket. Producers are now reluctant about sitting over songs, sharing context. If films have 12 music directors and 18 songwriters, how do you expect good work?” he said.When asked about the trend of recreating old songs, Sameer said there are both advantages and disadvantages to it, but there should be a limit.“The fact is that you cannot stop inventions. However, that is not the problem. Recreating a song has both pros and cons. Like when they remade my ‘Dilbar’ song, it got reintroduced to Gen Z. However, the problem starts when, while recreating a song, you ignore the original lyricist even when they are available and give the writing work to someone else, who then gives vulgar lines unrelated to the word ‘Dilbar’. They are insulting the literature. If you can improve something, please do. But don’t play with something to spoil the original,” he said.He added, “Morally, these people cannot touch this creative work without the permission of the original writers. Yet, they do it. This needs to stop. Good things work for a very long time. Good things will stay relevant for the next 100 years as well. People today assume that if a lyricist has become old, he might not be in touch with the pulse of today’s people. That’s not the case.”Sameer specifically criticised Dhurandhar for using old songs out of context, particularly during violent action sequences.“Films like Dhurandhar have made the situation even worse. Satyanash kar diya. They picked the music and put it in the background. In the trailer of Chauhan, they are playing Jumma Chumma during an action sequence. They recreated my song while they are firing guns. Where is the song?” he said.“My father doesn’t own the industry for me to make them stop. But this will continue until they ruin it all completely and then have nothing left. Nadeem tells me, ‘Pandit ji, you don’t worry. Just watch them quietly until they burn out everything we have. We will enter the picture after that,’” he added.Sameer also expressed disappointment with some of Bollywood’s biggest production houses.“I am more disappointed in the top banners owned by Aditya Chopra and Karan Johar. They used to patronise good music. I don’t understand what went wrong with them. They too don’t concentrate on music anymore,” he said.The Dhurandhar franchise, despite receiving mixed reviews, has reportedly earned over Rs 3,000 crore collectively from its two films.Sameer also criticised the practice of replacing experienced professionals with younger talent, while clarifying that he does not believe young artistes lack talent. Without naming the music company, he recalled an incident involving someone he knew.“This one time, someone I know told me that he had hired all young kids in his office. I was like, good. How long has it been? When he said about six years, I told him, ‘I have known your company for so long. There was a time when your company would release at least 10 superhit albums every year. How come you haven’t given a single hit in six years? Who exactly have you hired?’” he recalled. He clarified, “I am not saying that young kids are not talented. They are very talented, but I truly believe that if we merge the young with the old, it will give a great output.”Citing his own experience, Sameer said, “When I collaborated with Sachin-Nigam, I wrote ‘4 Baj Gaye Lekin Party Abhi Baki Hai’. With this song, I attempted to prove that when I can write songs like Faltu which young kids can relate to, what makes them assume I can’t? If you won’t give a chance to old composers and lyricists, how can you assume things?”Sameer further claimed that the industry’s increasing monotony was one of the reasons Arijit Singh distanced himself from the mainstream music industry.“It is this assumption that made Arijit Singh go crazy. Woh itna pagal ho gaya ki industry chhod ke chala gaya. Everything had become so monotonous. Same kind of songs and tunes. He understood that if he continued to do this, it would become monotonous for him. He couldn’t find his type of songs. There was no variety. When singers like Udit Narayan sang, they had so much variety. Any sensible man would quit,” he said.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Sydney Sweeney responde a las críticas por aparecer desnuda en un anuncio de apuestas: "Es día de juego"
articles.standfirst: La actriz desafía la polémica y publica nuevas imágenes de la campaña de Novig
articles.summary: La actriz desafía la polémica y publica nuevas imágenes de la campaña de Novig
articles.body: Sydney Sweeney no parece dispuesta a dar un paso atrás. La actriz ha respondido a las críticas que ha recibido por protagonizar completamente desnuda un provocador anuncio de Novig, una plataforma estadounidense de apuestas deportivas, con nuevas fotografías del rodaje y un escueto mensaje: "Es día de juego". En la campaña, la protagonista de 'La Asistenta' aparece sin ropa y cubriendo estratégicamente su cuerpo con pelotas, raquetas de tenis, balones de fútbol americano o sus propias manos. El anuncio pretende poner el foco en la fuerza, la belleza y la destreza vinculadas al deporte femenino, pero su puesta en escena ha provocado una fuerte reacción entre algunas atletas. La polémica surge precisamente porque varias deportistas consideran que la campaña reproduce la sexualización de las mujeres en un ámbito en el que llevan años reclamando ser valoradas por sus logros y no por su físico. Una de las críticas más contundentes ha llegado de la mano de Ariarne Titmus, cuatro veces medallista de oro olímpica. La exnadadora australiana mostró públicamente su indignación y aseguró que pensaba que este tipo de estrategia de marketing pertenecía al pasado. "No puedo describir lo indignada que me siento al ver esto", escribió en Instagram. Para Ariarne Titmus, la campaña supone "una bofetada en la cara" a las mujeres que han dedicado su vida a perfeccionar una disciplina deportiva, además de ignorar valores como el trabajo en equipo, la amistad, la dedicación, la excelencia y la unidad. La publicación de Sydney Sweeney también ha recibido críticas de otras mujeres, incluidas antiguas deportistas, que consideran que el anuncio contribuye a perpetuar una imagen sexualizada de las atletas. "Gracias por deshacer todo lo que las mujeres tratan de construir en los deportes" o "como ex atleta y mujer que ha experimentado personalmente comentarios sexualizados, estoy muy disgustada y profundamente decepcionada" son algunos de los comentarios que han generado debate. Lejos de retirar la campaña o pedir disculpas, Sydney Sweeney ha optado por redoblar su apuesta. La actriz ha publicado nuevas fotografías tomadas durante el rodaje, en la misma línea estética que las anteriores, acompañadas de un mensaje tan breve como desafiante: "Es día de juego". Además, en sus 'stories' ha compartido portadas y fotografías de conocidas deportistas, entre ellas Serena Williams, que también han protagonizado sesiones en las que posaban desnudas o con poca ropa para importantes medios de comunicación. La respuesta de Sydney Sweeney parece plantear así una cuestión de fondo: si una mujer deportista puede decidir posar desnuda y reivindicar su propio cuerpo, ¿por qué debería ser diferente cuando una actriz lo hace utilizando el imaginario del deporte? Para sus detractoras, sin embargo, el problema no está en la desnudez en sí, sino en utilizarla para vender un producto relacionado con las apuestas deportivas bajo el paraguas del empoderamiento femenino. No es la primera vez que Sydney Sweeney se encuentra en el centro de una controversia publicitaria. El año pasado, la actriz protagonizó una campaña de vaqueros construida alrededor del juego de palabras entre "jeans" y "genes" y de una referencia a su supuesta "buena genética". La campaña generó críticas por su posible lectura relacionada con el racismo, la eugenesia y el supremacismo blanco, debido a la utilización de características físicas como su cabello rubio, sus ojos azules o su complexión. La intérprete defendió entonces que la intención del anuncio era únicamente jugar con la similitud entre las palabras jeans y genes. Ahora, Sydney Sweeney vuelve a estar en el centro del debate. Y, al menos por el momento, su respuesta ante las críticas no ha sido dar explicaciones, sino publicar más imágenes y dejar claro que no piensa apartarse de la campaña.

articles.title: Sunita Ahuja breaks silence on Govinda's absence from Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations after cheating allegations: 'He's in America, but it's his house, he has to..'
articles.summary: Sunita Ahuja drew attention on Sunday after videos of her welcoming Ganpati Bappa home surfaced on social media. She was seen dancing and celebrating .
articles.body: Sunita Ahuja drew attention on Sunday after videos of her welcoming Ganpati Bappa home surfaced on social media. She was seen dancing and celebrating as the idol arrived, but one question kept coming up in the comments: where was Govinda?Sunita has now answered that. Speaking to ANI, she revealed that the actor is currently in America and is expected to return on Monday night.Addressing Govinda’s absence from the Ganpati celebrations, Sunita said he would return from America at night and could visit for darshan either the same day or the following day, depending on how tired he was after travelling.“Govinda ji is in America, he’ll come back at night. If he is tired, he won’t come for darshan today and instead will come tomorrow. This is his house, so he has to come," she said.Sunita also spoke about the family’s tradition of bringing Ganpati Bappa home every year. She shared that the custom was started by her mother-in-law and said she intends to continue following it for as long as she is alive.Usually, according to Sunita, either Govinda or their son Yashvardhan Ahuja brings the Ganpati idol home. This year, however, she decided to do it herself.“I brought Ganpati home this time with a lot of singing and dancing – usually, Govinda ji or Yashvardhan bring him," Sunita said.She also credited Ganpati Bappa for the developments in her life over the past year and explained why she wanted to personally bring the idol home this time. “In the last one year, Bappa has given me so much fame. articles.title: How Sandra Bullock’s Face Makes Her New Hit Movie Unwatchable
articles.summary: I have always loved Practical Magic. I saw it in theaters in 1998 with my mom and sister, and it has stayed with me ever since. I may or may not live in the...
articles.body:
I have always loved Practical Magic . I saw it in theaters in 1998 with my mom and sister, and it has stayed with me ever since. I may or may not live in the Pacific Northwest partially because of Practical Magic, which is set in Massachusetts but filmed in Washington. My wardrobe, hair, and cluttered home are all influenced by the Owens sisters. I watch the movie frequently, especially when I'm depressed or sick. It always makes me cry.

I saw the sequel, Practical Magic 2 , this weekend with my coven (two friends) and a theater full of women (and by my count, two men on dates). The audience audibly tittered during romantic moments, laughed at the sisterly banter, and clapped as the credits rolled. By the end of the weekend, it had unseated Spider-Man: Brand New Day as the number one movie at the box office with a $30 million haul.

There are a few reasons why it didn't hit for me. As Obsessed's Nick Schager outlined in his review , the script is clunky. I was willing to forgive the confusing timeline; the movie is almost 30 years old, and yet the girls from the first movie, who appeared to be about eight and 10, are only in their twenties now.

I get why it may make sense to recast beautiful 39-year-old Evan Rachel Wood, who played Kylie in the first movie, with (also beautiful) 27-year-old Joey King so we can watch a 20-something Kylie fight for her first love.

Beyond that, there are too many unnecessary special effects, and the soundtrack was pandering—I love the new Olivia Rodrigo album, but the climax set to "The Cure" didn't fit, and Alan Silvestri's soaring theme from the first movie, which is only heard during the denouement, didn't tug the heartstrings as it would have if it were woven throughout the film.

However, the main reason the second movie didn't move me was because of Sandra Bullock's unmoving face.

As Schager said, "Bullock is less than wholly expressive." But I don't think this is bad acting on Bullock's part. In the first movie, she played Sally Owens with a deadpan humor layered over deep grief. That worked for the tone of the role, especially in contrast with Nicole Kidman's Gillian, who is far more ebullient and dramatic.

Sally, who again is the protagonist of the ensemble film, is supposed to be uptight and repressed. In fact, an important plot point in the sequel involves Lee Pace's character helping stoic Sally "unblock" her magic. He places a hand over her heart and, after a random special effect ripple and instrumental flourish, he says, "That should do it," meaning that Sally is now free of her constraints. But there was no visible change in Bullock.

Bullock, who is 62, appears to have botoxed, lifted, or otherwise plasticized her gorgeous face into a mask of her former self, transforming her into a Madame Tussauds wax statue of Sandra Bullock. We can tell who she's supposed to be, but it's not quite right.

Sally's massive witchy power and emotion that surges through her can't ever leak out, not even when her daughter is in mortal peril or when she's falling in love with suave Pace (cue lady in my theater letting out a "woo!").

In Pace's scenes, I found myself staring into the crevasse that is the one line running between his eyes, which conveys a pathos and longing I first fell in love with during Pushing Daisies , nearly 20 years ago. Pace is 47, meaning we have a 15-year age gap here. Yet Bullock's uncanny agelessness muddies the believability of them as a couple not because of their age difference but because she can no longer convey chemistry.

In contrast, when the camera was on Bullock, I felt like Nathan Fielder in the Elizabeth Holmes documentary , staring into an emotionless, wrinkle-free face, not believing that the words coming out of Bullock's mouth could possibly be true. The lack of eyebrow musculature robs her performance of any nuance, which forces her to play up physical comedy (which she's still great at) and rely heavily on the weak script and effects to carry her through.

Nicole Kidman's face moved ever so slightly more, and she had less of an acting challenge, a playful sprite to Bullock's stoic mom in crisis. But Kidman certainly doesn't look 59. Dianne Wiest looks more ethereal than ever while still looking her age (78). Stockard Channing, 81 and looking like she's had some work done too, is at least allowed a wild river of white in her hair.

In the first movie, the "old aunts" played by Channing and Wiest were in their early fifties, had hair streaked with gray and wrinkles mapping expressive topographies on their faces. How the times have changed…

The double standard here is clear: Pace gets to have a wrinkle between his eyebrows, but Bullock doesn't. It's not fair that Bullock feels like she has to look like she did in her mid-thirties. I believe people should have body autonomy and do whatever they want to make themselves feel good and, in the case of these actors, to survive in a brutal industry.

But on the other hand, catharsis should be a primary job of art and the artist. I cry during the first movie because I identify with Sally's heartbreak and feel empathy for her. An actor's responsibility is to help the audience feel feelings, to give them an outlet for grief, love, and longing. If I can't read an actor's face, I cannot feel what they want me to feel.

Of course, it may be that I'm just being petty, judging other women on their appearance instead of, as the movie tells us to do, banding together with my fellow witches to overcome patriarchal systems that aim to harm us.

I'd like to think I'm giving permission, not that anyone asked me, for actors to age gracefully, to show us a mirror of what a long life actually looks like, not the overly-smooth facade Hollywood thinks we want to see.

The women/witches in the Practical Magic universe have an enviable connection to nature, each other, and their own selves—their love is real and deep. I wish I had the power to see that real, deep love play out on their faces.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Helen Mirren: 'I believe that if you want to go make your mark on the world, you’ve got to go out and do it. Don’t be shy, be adventurous,' a powerful life lesson on courage, ambition and leaving an impression with your actions
articles.summary: Discover the powerful message from Helen Mirren about taking risks and leaving your mark on the world. Learn how to embrace opportunities and overcome hesitation for personal and professional growth.
articles.body: Some opportunities look exciting from a distance. When the moment finally arrives, though, it can be surprisingly easy to talk yourself out of taking it. Doubts start creeping in; you wonder whether you are ready and suddenly staying where you are feels much safer. Helen Mirren’s career offers an interesting take on that feeling; sometimes you have to stop overthinking and simply give yourself a chance.Helen Mirren's career offers an interesting perspective on that hesitation. The actress has spent decades moving between theatre, television and film, taking on roles that have challenged her at different stages of her life. Her advice is equally direct: if you want to leave your mark, you cannot spend too much time waiting for the perfect moment.Today’s quote of the day by Helen Mirren reads: “I believe that if you want to go make your mark on the world, you’ve got to go out and do it. Don’t be shy, be adventurous.”What does the quote by Helen Mirren mean?Helen Mirren shared this thought in a 2015 conversation with Jan Janssen of The Interview Feed, published in the Wisconsin Gazette while she was promoting ‘Woman in Gold’. During the interview, Mirren was asked about the confidence she appeared to have and whether people found her scary. Her answer eventually led to a reflection on how she had changed from the insecure young woman she once was.Mirren's message is simple: if you want something from life, there comes a point when you have to stop waiting and take action. Being adventurous in this context does not mean making reckless choices; it referes to taking a chance by trying something new.Mirren spoke about lacking confidence when she was young and learning to become more comfortable with herself. Her words therefore come from someone who understands that confidence does not always appear overnight. Sometimes, it develops because a person keeps putting themselves in situations that once made them uncomfortable.How is the quote by Helen Mirren relevant today?Hesitation is something almost everyone can relate to. A student may wonder whether they are good enough to apply for an opportunity. In professional life, people think twice before speaking their mind, as they don't want to risk their job.Mirren’s words suggest that you may never feel fully prepared before making an important move. There are moments when you have to take the risk first and figure things out. That first step might feel uncertain, but it could lead you toward an opportunity you would have missed by staying where you were.Early life of Helen MirrenHelen Mirren was born in London on July 26, 1945. She fell in love with acting at a young age and later, following her heart, she joined the National Youth Theatre. Her time there led to opportunities with the Royal Shakespeare Company, where she took on a variety of roles and began building her reputation as a serious stage actress.Much of Mirren’s early work was on the theatre stage. She later worked with Peter Brook’s theatre company and travelled internationally with productions, gaining experience that proved useful as she moved between theatre, film and television.Helen Mirren’s rise to fameMirren's success was built over many years rather than arriving with one defining early role. She appeared in films such as ‘Age of Consent’, ‘The Long Good Friday’, ‘Excalibur’, ‘Cal’ and ‘The Cook, the Thief, His Wife & Her Lover’.Television eventually introduced her to an even wider audience. Her portrayal of Detective Chief Inspector Jane Tennison in ‘Prime Suspect’ became one of the most important roles of her career and brought her widespread recognition.‘The Queen’ became another turning point in Mirren’s career. "His work with Carol Burnett and the ensemble of ‘The Carol Burnett Show,’ with Cher starting with ‘The Sonny & Cher Comedy Hour,’ as well as with Joan Rivers, Bette Midler and Lucille Ball, helped shape some of comedy’s most memorable moments on television and stage." articles.title: Macklemore says he was dropped from Ed Sheeran tour after Patriots owner Robert Kraft organized boycott
articles.summary: Macklemore has been dropped from Ed Sheeran’s tour after he says New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft organized a boycott among stadium owners over the rapper’s remarks in support of Palestinians.
articles.body: Macklemore has been dropped from Ed Sheeran’s tour after he says New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft organized a boycott among stadium owners over the rapper’s remarks in support of Palestinians. The “Thrift Shop” rapper posted a lengthy statement to his Instagram on Monday alleging that Sheeran was called by Kraft to inform the singer Macklemore was not welcome at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. Sheeran’s tour was scheduled to play at the venue, which is owned by Kraft Entertainment + Sports Group. “Ed also told me that Kraft had rallied some of the other stadium owners and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: if Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues,” Macklemore wrote. The decision was reached after comments made by Macklemore at the tour’s New Jersey shows and “a broader history of rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community,” Kraft said in a statement provided to NBC News on Monday. Gillette Stadium seeks to create a “welcoming environment for all guests,” he added. “I would welcome the opportunity to sit down with Macklemore and discuss the facts, because ultimately our goal is the same — peace for all people, an end to suffering, and an end to all hate,” Kraft said. He added that that the decision was not about trying to stifle Palestinian advocacy or diminishing the suffering of Palestinians. Kraft blamed Hamas, a designated terrorist organization, for the actions that “have caused immeasurable suffering for Palestinians and Israelis alike.” “Much of my time and attention for the last decade has been focused on the fight against antisemitism and hate of all kinds, and I feel a responsibility to stand up when I believe that line has been crossed,” Kraft said. Kraft, who is Jewish, created the Foundation to Combat Antisemitism in 2019 and is a longtime supporter of Israel. There is a page dedicated to his Israel-related philanthropic efforts on the Kraft Group’s site. “The Kraft family has supported and launched numerous programs that create a connection to Israel and Jewish life,” the site said. “Their commitment has helped build a robust economic relationship between Boston and Israel, the results of which have created jobs and fostered technological innovations in both communities.” Macklemore added that Sheeran, who he described as a friend, was in a “f---ed up position.” The two have had “difficult” conversations over the past week, according to Macklemore, that ended in a place of “fundamental disagreement.” “He told me that the words ‘Free Palestine’ and the image of the Palestinian flags were hurtful to a lot of people he spoke with,” Macklemore wrote. “I told him that if those words were more offensive than the tens of thousands of Palestinian children being killed by Israel, then there was a fundamental disconnect between where those people stood and where I stood.” According to Macklemore’s account, Sheeran was not able to get past his desire to remain an apolitical public figure. Macklemore has been deeply outspoken about social and political issues throughout his career, releasing the song 2012 song “Same Love” in support of same-sex marriage three years before it was legalized in a Supreme Court decision. He released a song called “Hind’s Hall” in 2024, referencing an anti-war protest at Columbia University in which students took over a building and renamed in honor of 6-year-old Palestinian girl killed in Gaza. “The problem isn’t the protests, it’s what they’re protesting,” the song lyrics say. “It goes against what our country is funding.” He performed the song while opening for Sheeran at Metlife Stadium in New Jersey earlier this month. According to video posted by Macklemore, he told the crowd that part of why he wanted to be on the tour was to be able to be in stadiums to say “Free Palestine.” The clip of Macklemore drew controversy and criticism, including from fellow artist Pink, who identifies as Jewish. She put out a statement on Friday explaining why she reposted a social media post critical of Macklemore’s performance. She wrote that she was not trying to get any artist fired or silence anyone, but she took issue with Macklemore putting “violent images” of the Israel-Hamas War up in a stadium filled with families and then telling Jews in the audience that “it wasn’t about them.” “You don’t get to decide that for us,” she wrote Friday. “That’s what prompted my repost. Not ‘Free Palestine,’ and not anyone’s right to say it.” Representatives for Pink and Sheeran did not immediately responded to a request for comment on Monday. The company working on Sheeran’s tour, Messina Touring Group, told Rolling Stone on Monday that they were informed that multiple venues “will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup.” Cancellations would “impact hundreds of thousands of fans,” the statement said, confirming that Macklemore would not longer perform on his previously scheduled dates. Macklemore told his followers that he is not a victim, nor are Pink or Sheeran. He wrote that the victims are the Palestinian people who have been “forced to live through unimaginable violence.” He also said he understood why many people do not take a side, but pointed out that he has been outspoken in his position for three years prior to the tour. The decision to remain outspoken about the war has become something Macklemore said he considers a duty. “An entire people being displaced, starved, and killed while the world debates which words we allowed to use to describe it, how those words make us feel, and whether our discomfort matters ore than the people living through a genocide,” he wrote. Hamas-led attacks on Israel on Oct. 7, 2023, killed about 1,200 people and saw 250 others taken hostage, prompting a multiyear war offensive by Israel into Gaza. More than 73,000 people in Gaza have died as a result of Israel’s attacks in the enclave, according to the Palestinian Health Ministry. A ceasefire was declared in October, though fighting has still occurred since the announcement.

She tied the knot with Irish-Australian financier Cameron O’Reilly, 62, over the weekend, with the marriage confirmed by members of her family.The wedding comes more than two decades after Jemima’s divorce from Imran Khan. The couple, who married in 1995, ended their nine-year marriage in 2004.Jemima Goldsmith’s family confirms weddingConfirmation of the marriage came not from the newlyweds themselves but from Jemima’s sister-in-law, Jemima Jones, who is married to her brother Ben Goldsmith.On September 13, Jones shared a photograph on Instagram showing what appeared to be an estate with manicured lawns and a lily pond. She captioned the post, “Celebrating Jemima and Cameron’s wedding, with my favourite date, what a happy day!”Jemima’s brother Ben Goldsmith also confirmed that the couple had married.According to reports, Jemima and Cameron had been friends for some time before their relationship turned romantic. The pair are understood to have met through work while Cameron was working as an executive producer on documentaries and films.A previous report from the Daily Mail stated that the couple had been together for just over a year after initially being friends.Who is Cameron O’Reilly?Cameron O’Reilly, 62, is the son of the late Irish media magnate and international rugby star Sir Anthony O’Reilly. He spent around a decade working in his father’s media empire, Independent News & Media, before later joining Australian group APN News & Media.He stepped down as chief executive in 2000 and went on to establish private equity fund Bayard Capital in 2003. The firm acquired Swiss metering company Landis+Gyr, where Cameron served as chief executive. The company was later sold to Toshiba for $2.3 billion in 2011.Cameron has four children, while Jemima has two sons, Sulaiman and Kasim, from her marriage to Imran Khan.Jemima and Imran Khan’s marriageJemima married Imran Khan in 1995 when she was 21. She and her sons have also campaigned for Imran Khan’s release from prison.Imran Khan remains in prisonImran Khan, the former Pakistan cricket captain who went on to become the country’s prime minister, has been imprisoned since 2023 in connection with corruption cases that he denies and has described as politically motivated.Jemima and her sons have repeatedly spoken about his imprisonment and his health. His lawyers have also raised concerns over his condition in custody.The former prime minister has faced several legal cases and remains behind bars, while his family and supporters continue to call for his release.Jemima Goldsmith’s career in filmJemima has established a successful career as a film and television producer and documentary maker. She has also remained a prominent public figure in Britain and has previously been known for her friendship with the late Princess Diana.Her second marriage comes nearly a year after the death of her mother, Lady Annabel Goldsmith, the celebrated British socialite after whom the famous Annabel’s nightclub in London’s Mayfair was named.Jemima’s father, billionaire businessman Sir James Goldsmith, died in 1997.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Alaska moose hunter miraculously survives ambush brown bear attack, says he 'blacked out'
articles.summary: Gavin Haakenson was charging a brown bear from 10 feet away near Alaska's Killey River when his friend's pistol shots saved him from the attack.
articles.body: A moose hunter in Alaska somehow walked away from a brown bear attack with little more than a shredded jacket, a bruised shoulder and one hell of a story. Gavin Haakenson was scouting for moose with his friend Ethan Yeager near Alaska’s Killey River on Sept. 2 when a brown bear came charging at him from roughly 10 feet away. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS "I heard a noise to my right and looked over and there was a brown bear charging me at full speed," Haakenson told Outdoor Life. "It was super close, maybe 10 feet, when I saw it. It was growling extremely loud, a terrifying noise. I saw its face. Its teeth were out. It hit me in the shoulder and knocked me down." And then Haakenson’s memory cuts out. "Last thing I remember was trying to shoulder my rifle and the bear jumping at me," he said. "Then I don’t remember what happened. That’s when my black out started." Yeager fired his pistol as Haakenson was trapped underneath the bear. The animal eventually got off him and ran away as Yeager continued firing. "The whole thing happened in under 10 seconds," Haakenson said. "Then we hiked back to the truck as fast as we could yelling, ‘hey bear’ with some fear in our voices." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Somehow, Haakenson escaped without broken bones or major wounds. The bear tore through his coat and left him bruised and sore, while his rifle also took some damage. WILDLIFE PHOTOGRAPHER STAYS ICE-COLD AS MASSIVE BROWN BEAR WALKS RIGHT UP TO HIS CAMERA Considering what could have happened, though, he’s almost grateful he doesn’t remember the worst part. "I get restless just thinking about it," Haakenson said. "I’m glad I blacked out and don’t remember the bear being on top of me. The thought of ‘what if’ is what keeps me up." Wildlife officers later searched the area but did not find the bear. Haakenson, meanwhile, hasn’t completely ruled out going back. articles.title: Why Bob Mackie didn't want Kim Kardashian in Marilyn Monroe's dress
articles.summary: Legendary fashion designer Bob Mackie was opposed to Kim Kardashian wearing the Marilyn Monroe dress for the 2022 Met Gala. Here's why.
articles.body:
Bob Mackie had strong feelings about Kim Kardashian wearing Marilyn Monroe's historic dress .

The legendary fashion designer, whose death was announced Sept. 14 at age 87, sketched the original design at the start of his career while working as an assistant to French-born costumer Jean Louis.

Monroe made American history in 1962 when she wore the nude shimmering gown during her performance of "Happy Birthday" for then-President John F. Kennedy. The dress and her serenade were never forgotten.

So much so that 60 years later in 2022, Kardashian worked with the owner of the dress, Ripley's Believe It or Not! museum, to wear the bling-encrusted gown to the Met Gala, acknowledging that she slimmed down dramatically to fit into it.

Mackie called Kardashian's wearing of the skin-tight gown a "big mistake," telling Entertainment Weekly that Monroe was "a goddess. A crazy goddess, but a goddess." He went on to describe her as "just fabulous," noting that the dress "was designed for her."

The dress, custom made for Monroe, was adorned with more than 2,500 crystals.

Mackie, who was just 21 when he drew the design, made his opinion clear: "Nobody else should be seen in that dress."

It wasn't just Mackie who expressed concern over Kardashian donning the dress. Many others, including art conservators and historians, slammed the reality star for wearing a historic archival item, citing concerns for the gown's fragility.

"I am so honored to be wearing the iconic dress that Marilyn Monroe wore in 1962," Kardashian wrote on Instagram at the time, describing the item as "an evocative piece of fashion history."

Kardashian explained that the Met Gala's theme, "Gilded Glamour," prompted her to look into hunting down the iconic dress. "For me, the most Marilyn Monroe moment is when she sang "Happy Birthday," to JFK, it was that look," she told Vogue.

Kardashian wore the dress up the Met Gala steps briefly before slipping into a replica, though she was later accused of permanently damaging the gown , an expert closely familiar with the dress told USA TODAY at the time.

The garment's zipper appeared to be damaged and the famed gown showed signs of stress on its shoulder straps, as well as missing beads and sequins, according to ChadMichael Morrisette, a visual artist who curates museum and costume exhibits.

Kardashian later denied damaging the dress, saying that she wore it for less than five minutes and that handlers wearing gloves helped her get into it.

The Ripley's Believe It or Not! museum also denied the star had caused any damage to the item while wearing it.

"From the bottom of the Met steps, where Kim got into the dress, to the top where it was returned, the dress was in the same condition it started in," Amanda Joiner, Ripley's vice president of publishing and licensing, said in a statement at the time.

Mackie was famous for his signature embellished and beaded designs for icons including Cher, Dolly Parton, Tina Turner and Diana Ross.

"His genius and extraordinary designs will live on forever, continuing to bring beauty into this world," Mackie's team wrote in their tribute to him on Monday.

articles.title: Lucas González desvela cómo evoluciona su nariz tras su última revisión: "Va más lento de lo esperado"
articles.standfirst: El cantante ha hablado con ‘Y ahora Sonsoles’, de Antena 3
articles.summary: El cantante ha hablado con ‘Y ahora Sonsoles’, de Antena 3
articles.body: Este lunes, 14 de septiembre, Lucas González ha reaparecido para contar cómo evoluciona su nariz tras su última revisión. El cantante ha hablado con ‘Y ahora Sonsoles’, el espacio de Antena 3 presentado por Sonsoles Ónega, donde ha revelado que la recuperación va un poco más lenta de lo esperado. El exintegrante del dúo Andy y Lucas ha señalado que los médicos prefieren que lleve los retenedores un poco más de tiempo de lo previsto inicialmente para asegurar que la estructura evolucione de forma correcta. "Tengo que volver a finales de octubre para quitarme los retenedores. Me han hecho tenerlos un poquito más para que se sostenga bien, como Dios manda", detallaba. Aunque la evolución es pausada, el artista se muestra muy ilusionado y satisfecho con los cambios estéticos logrados tras la compleja reconstrucción nasal a la que se sometió en Turquía. "Me veo que tengo perfil, que antes no tenía. Es una pesadilla que he pasado en mi vida", afirmaba, visiblemente contento tras esta nueva operación provocada por una mala recuperación durante la primera. Por otro lado, Lucas ha reconocido que todavía experimenta algunas molestias físicas lógicas y que debe mantener un cuidado estricto en su día a día para evitar complicaciones. Además, ha comentado que no puede coger “ninguna infección" porque sería muy perjudicial para el proceso. Una de sus mayores preocupaciones era el canto, pero ha confirmado que la intervención no ha afectado en absoluto a su voz, la cual siente en perfecto estado. Para ver los resultados definitivos de esta segunda cirugía reconstructiva, el gaditano tendrá que esperar todavía un periodo de entre cuatro y cinco meses.

His genius and extraordinary designs will live on forever, continuing to bring beauty into this world.”Known for his dazzling, theatrical creations, Mackie became one of the most influential designers in American entertainment. His work was closely associated with some of the biggest stars in music and television, including Cher, Miley Cyrus, Diana Ross, Carol Burnett, Bette Midler, Liza Minnelli and RuPaul.Celebrities pay tributeAmong the celebrities paying tribute to Mackie was singer Sabrina Carpenter, who had worn several of his creations.“I feel so lucky to have met Bob,” Carpenter wrote on her Instagram Stories. “His one of a kind creations have inspired and brought so much happiness and confidence to my world and they will continue to always x Mackie girl forever.”Model Coco Rocha also remembered Mackie, praising the lasting influence of his work.“There are designers whose work defines a moment, and then there are those rare few whose imagination teaches fashion something for generations. Bob was one of them. His clothes had wit, drama, fantasy and joy,” she wrote.Miley Cyrus wrote, "The legendary Bob Mackie has passed away at 87. Rest in peace, grace and fashion. Thank you for your art."Actress Alyssa Milano shared her condolences on social media, describing Mackie as “one of the best that ever was” and revealing that she owns a collection of his dresses.Fifth Harmony alum Lauren Jauregui wrote, “Rest in peace to beautiful master of his craft. Thank you for all the beauty, Bob.”Michelle Visage also paid tribute to the designer, writing, “WE LOVE YOU BOB!!!! We will never EVER forget you and we are all eternally grateful for your art.”Laverne Cox remembered Mackie with a brief but heartfelt message, “Rest in Power. Thank you Mr. Mackie.”RuPaul's Drag Race alum Shea Coulee wrote, “So thankful to you Bob for all of the glamour and beauty you’ve gifted the world. Rest in peace.”Designer Christian Cowan called Mackie a “Forever icon of design and joy”, while British-American designer Harris Reed described him as a “True visionary.”Mickey Boardman, longtime editorial director of PAPER magazine, remembered Mackie as “A true legend and an incredibly nice man,” adding that his work had been a gift to his iconic clients and audiences everywhere.The Lennon Sisters remember MackieKathy Lennon of vocal group The Lennon Sisters also shared a tribute on Facebook, remembering Mackie as a talented and welcoming figure.She wrote that Mackie had “left his legacy forever in the iconic world of gowns and show piece costumes,” adding that he was “one in a million” and would be “terribly missed, and never forgotten.”Bob Mackie’s legendary careerBorn Robert Gordon Mackie on March 24, 1939, in Monterey Park, California, Mackie developed an interest in fashion and costume design at an early age. He attended Pasadena City College and later studied at the Chouinard Art Institute before leaving to work at Paramount Studios.From 1960 to 1963, he worked as an assistant and emerging designer under Ray Aghayan at Paramount Studios.Mackie went on to build an extraordinary career in television, film and fashion. He served as the costume designer for all 11 seasons of The Carol Burnett Show, which ran from 1967 to 1978, and later designed costumes for Mama's Family. He also worked on The Sonny and Cher Show and created numerous costumes for Cher's concert tours.His designs became synonymous with glamour, extravagance and theatricality. He dressed stars including Cher, Diana Ross, Barbara Eden, RuPaul, Bette Midler, Liza Minnelli, Judy Garland, Joan Rivers and Tina Turner.Awards and legacyMackie's work earned him nine Primetime Emmy Awards, a Tony Award and three Academy Award nominations. He was inducted into the Television Hall of Fame in 2002.In 1982, Mattel introduced a collection of collectible Bob Mackie Barbies, while Mackie later launched the QVC Wearable Art Collection in the 1990s.Over the course of his career, Mackie transformed celebrity dressing into a form of theatrical storytelling, leaving behind a legacy that continues to influence designers and performers.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.body:
Serie A side Milan 's owner Gerry Cardinale is looking to expand his football empire and considerations are being made to include Al Nassr into the network.

In Serie A, Roma are a classic example of multi-club ownership, as the Friedkins are also owners of Everton . Another example is that of Udinese , where the Pozzo family also own Watford in the Championship. Milan have also followed that plan, with Cardinale also owning French side Toulouse .

Gianluigi Longari reports that the Rossoneri do not intend to stop at Toulouse. Discussions have been held with Al Nassr to have the Saudi side under the RedBird network.

Contacts were made indirectly and the idea has been assessed by the two clubs. For now, the task appears to be uphill but Cardinale is evaluating the idea of making this possible.

There is every reason Jorge Mendes is playing a big role in this. The Portuguese has been closely working with Cardinale in the last few months over incomings and outgoings and has excellent contacts in the Middle East.

articles.title: Roma Makes It Four Straight With Workmanlike Win at Torino
articles.summary: Roma’s momentum just can’t be halted right now, with a 2-0 win over Torino their latest triumph in Serie A.
articles.body:
Another week, another win. Roma 's momentum just can't be halted right now in Serie A, with a 2-0 win over Torino representing a positive return to league action after Thursday's Champions League draw with Fenerbahçe.

Roma are now four from four in Serie A and they've been winning in a variety of ways. There were the comprehensive thrashings of Fiorentina and Lecce , before the late comeback of a smash-and-grab win over Atalanta . And against Torino, it was another category of win.

This was more of a grind-it-out kind of victory: not the easiest game on the eye at times, but one Roma were able to prevail from.

The opening exchanges were fairly open and stretched, with both teams vying for control of the ball. It took until the 10th minute for the first half-chance, when an inviting cross from Mario Hermoso was headed over by Donyell Malen .

Malen then saw a first-time shot from outside the box deflected wide a couple of minutes later, having latched onto a loose ball after Matías Soulé had overrun in possession of the ball.

Soon, it began to become clear what kind of challenge Roma were in for. Even in the first half, Torino were pulling out timewasting tactics; you got the feeling they'd have been content for a goalless draw. But Roma weren't having any of it.

There was a faint chance of a breakthrough when some stepovers by Emanuele Lulli got the better of the Torino defence, before his low cross almost caused an own goal when the ball was diverted away.

The Torino net was breached shortly after, when Paulo Dybala played through Malen for the Dutchman to let rip, but he was offside.

It was that combination that unlocked the game for good, though. Dybala won't be officially credited with the assist because of Torino breaking it up, but it was he who put Malen in. A bit of persistence and Roma's leading scorer of 2026 was able to prod the ball home yet again.

From that point on, Torino couldn't take their time as much anymore, but the second half didn't fully open up and was once again characterised by half-chances, neither keeper having too many tough saves to make.

Nahuel Molina , starting at left-back in place of Wesley and doing a pretty good job, had a couple of efforts, firing one just over after being set up by Malen and later forcing Lucas Perri to push away his powerful effort.

In between those chances, Mile Svilar made a routine save from a Rolando Mandragora free kick, and Bryan Cristante skied a left-footed shot.

As the closing stretches approached, it became a case of managing the game for Roma, but they still had their moments – usually driven by, paradoxically, defender Gianluca Mancini .

Having inherited the captain's armband from Cristante, Mancini had an attempt with a header after a cross from Rodrigo Mora, but he couldn't generate enough power.

His forward-thinking approach paid off in stoppage time, though, when he kept it alive on the touchline to craft a late chance in the box. The ball eventually fell to Niccolò Pisilli , who made it 2-0 with a powerful effort across goal.

Just like in the opening game against Fiorentina, Pisilli – who was making his first start of the season, and ran more than anyone else on the pitch – popped up with a late goal to finish off the tie. This time, considering Roma only had a one-goal advantage at the time, it was far more important in settling the score.

So there we had it: another three points in the bag for Roma. It's the first time since 2014-15 that they've won their first four league matches in a season.

Roma are still on their perch at the top of the table thanks to their latest win, and the excitement around this team is certainly building. This was a professional performance, when Roma didn't need to be at their blistering best but no player really had an off day. Being able to bed in the likes of Molina, Pisilli and first-time starter Leonardo Balerdi was another positive, as was getting Malen back on the scoresheet after two games without a goal (a drought by his standards). Lots to be content with, then, but Roma quickly have to reset ahead of their biggest challenge of the season yet.

It's the big one. Roma host Inter on Saturday, which – depending on the Nerazzurri's result against Udinese later on Monday – could well be first versus second.

articles.title: Macklemore doubles down after getting kicked off Ed Sheeran tour after pro-Palestine stance
articles.summary: Macklemore claims Robert Kraft rallied stadium owners to give Ed Sheeran an ultimatum over his "Free Palestine" remarks on the U.S. Loop Tour.
articles.body: A week after Macklemore repeatedly called to "Free Palestine" and performed his anti-Israel song "Hind’s Hall" while opening for Ed Sheeran, the rapper was dropped from the remaining U.S. dates he was scheduled to perform on the "Shape of You" singer's "Loop Tour." "As the concert promoter for Ed Sheeran’s U.S. Loop Tour, we have been notified by venues on the upcoming U.S. tour dates that they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup, which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans," Messina Touring Group, the promoter of the U.S. leg of Sheeran’s Loop Tour, said in a statement to Rolling Stone. "After discussions with stakeholders, Macklemore will not be performing on the remaining support dates." Macklemore was slated to appear at eight of the 10 shows left on the U.S. leg of Sheeran’s tour. PINK HITS BACK AMID BACKLASH FOR CRITICIZING MACKLEMORE'S PRO-PALESTINIAN CONCERT REMARKS On Monday, Macklemore addressed the announcement and doubled down on his stance. "I’m not sure how to start this. So I’m going to speak from the heart and share the truth," he wrote in a lengthy Instagram statement. "Ed Sheeran and his team have made the decision to remove me from The Loop tour. But before I get into it, I want to say something that should be obvious. In this moment I think it matters. I am not a victim. Ed Sheeran is not a victim. Pink is not a victim. We have careers, money, opportunities, safety and audiences around the world. Whatever consequences any of us face for what we say, we get to go home to our families." BILL MAHER RIPS MACKLEMORE'S GAZA STANCE, SAYS CELEBRITY 'MORAL CONFUSION' IS FUELING ANTISEMITISM "The victims are the Palestinian people. The men, women and children who have been killed, starved, displaced and forced to live through unimaginable violence. More than 20,000 children have been killed in Gaza alone. People are being killed today, and people will be killed tomorrow. I want to make sure that as I tell this story, we don’t lose sight of that." WATCH: MACKLEMORE OPENED HIS PERFORMANCE WITH AN ANTI-ICE AND ISRAEL RANT On Sept. 4, Macklemore opened for Sheeran at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. He repeatedly chanted "Free Palestine" while a slideshow played on the screen behind him, showing footage from the war in Gaza. Several fans were upset by the performance, including an Instagram page called "Stop Antisemitism." The page shared a video criticizing Macklemore, calling the move "awful." Pink reposted the video to her own Instagram story, which started a new wave of backlash from people criticizing her for seemingly being pro-Israel. In his Instagram post, Macklemore said he and Sheeran, who he considers a "friend" and "brother," had "some difficult conversations" in the days following his remarks. "The type of talks rooted in love and respect for one another that still end in a place of fundamental disagreement," he wrote. "Nothing I’m writing here is out of spite or because I want to tear down his character. But as I told Ed multiple times on the phone, our friendship can’t change my responsibility to tell the truth about what happened." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE The rapper claimed Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium, told Sheeran that Macklemore "would not be allowed" to perform at the stadium. Kraft issued a statement defending his decision to influence the rapper's removal from the tour. "Gillette Stadium has a longstanding commitment to providing a welcoming environment for all guests and ensuring that events held at our venue do not provide a platform for hate speech," the statement read. "Based on Macklemore’s recent actions, material shared from the stage during Ed Sheeran’s shows in New Jersey, and a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community, we determined that his participation in the September 25th and 26th concerts at Gillette Stadium would cross that line." The statement continued: "This decision is not about diminishing the suffering of innocent Palestinians or denying anyone the right to advocate on their behalf. Their pain and loss are real. But that advocacy should not come at the expense of the Jewish community or obscure the responsibility of Hamas, a United States and globally (including Canada, European Union, United Kingdom, and Japan) designated terrorist organization whose horrific actions have caused immeasurable suffering for Palestinians and Israelis alike. I agree with Macklemore. Too many lives have been lost and there has been too much suffering, but only sharing selective information and ignoring the actions of Hamas is not honest and only advances more divisiveness and hate. Over many decades, I have directed resources to Palestine and created athletic and entrepreneurial opportunities for Palestinians who I admire and respect. Standing with the Palestinian people and standing against Hamas, antisemitism and hate should not be mutually exclusive. "Much of my time and attention for the last decade has been focused on the fight against antisemitism and hate of all kinds, and I feel a responsibility to stand up when I believe that line has been crossed. I have tremendous respect for Ed and his music, particularly his unique ability to bring people together and spread joy, and I have always been proud to welcome him and his fans to Gillette Stadium. "I would welcome the opportunity to sit down with Macklemore and discuss the facts, because ultimately our goal is the same – peace for all people, an end to suffering, and an end to all hate." In Macklemore's post, he said, "Ed also told me that Kraft had rallied some of the other stadium owners and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: if Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "Ed was in a f---ed up position," he wrote. "He knew it. His typical apolitical stance was being challenged in a way it never had been before. He told me that the words 'Free Palestine' and the image of the Palestinian flag were hurtful to a lot of people he spoke with. I told him that if those words were more offensive than tens of thousands of Palestinian children being killed by Israel, then there was a fundamental disconnect between where those people stood and where I stood. But he couldn’t get past his public facing, 'I don’t take sides.'" WATCH: PINK SLAMS MACKLEMORE OVER PRO-PALESTINIAN COMMENTS CHRIS ROBINSON, BRUCE SPRINGSTEEN FACE BACKLASH AS 'AMERICANS HAVE HAD ENOUGH' OF BEING LECTURED: EXPERT Macklemore said he's been saying "Free Palestine" onstage for almost three years and questioned why he was being removed from the tour now. "What I said at MetLife I have been saying on stages around the world for almost three years. So why is it an issue now? Because now I’m sharing a stage with one of the biggest artists in the world, in some of the biggest stadiums in America. At a certain level of exposure, ‘Free Palestine’ becomes too much of a risk. If I kept doing the shows, saying ‘Free Palestine,’ with Ed implicitly supporting it, the crowd getting loud and showing undeniable support for Palestinian liberation, what artist might speak out next? The stage becomes resistance. Maybe that’s why this time it became so important to silence me." Antisemitism is real," he continued. "And that is exactly why the word matters too much to be used as a shield against criticism of the Israeli state. When criticizing Israel, opposing Zionism or saying ‘Free Palestine’ gets conflated with hatred of Jewish people, it doesn’t protect Jewish people. It protects Israel from accountability." While Macklemore said he hopes his relationship with Sheeran won't crumble over this, he said he stands by his position. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I didn’t need 10 shows from Ed. LONDON – Prince Harry and Duchess Meghan are pulling their children out of their new school.

Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5 , started at their new school in Britain just days ago but are now having to switch to another one amid ongoing security concerns.

The Sussex family moved back to Britain last month after six years in the United States.

"The decision for the children to move school was taken following a discussion with the family's security team about the practicalities of their current arrangements," a representative for the couple told USA TODAY on Monday, Sept. 14.

"The parents remain extremely grateful to all the teachers and staff for the love, care and effort they have shown their family," the representative said. "This decision should in no way be interpreted as a reflection on the school or the exceptional care the children have received there."

Hello! Magazine , citing sources close to the couple, reported that there was no issue with the school itself, but that problems were already beginning to emerge when it came to the school drop-off and pick up.

The children are expected to start at another school in the area soon.

The news comes a day after Meghan, 45, shared a string of photos to Instagram on Sept. 13 showing a rare glimpse of what their new life away from California looks like. The photos showed the family fishing, walking in woodlands and wearing raincoats and wellington boots.
